messages:
sam: proposing a small change to how we track postmortem actions — introduce a 'remediation queue' and batch owners into sprintlets to reduce churn and make SLAs explicit. idea below.

aya: love this. can you outline how it affects IC rotation? :eyes:

sam: short thread: 1) remediation queue (single list prioritized by severity & recurrence), 2) sprintlets (3-day owner sprints for medium/low), 3) owner micro-rotation (weekly pool), 4) comm windows (ack/triage/fix windows)

mike: curious about metrics — how do we avoid piling up low-severity items? propose auto-archive rule + backlog cap.

lisa: suggested comm cadence: 2h triage ack for P1, 24h ack for P2, 7d target for P1 fix, 21d for P2. also include weekly 'health' digest.

sam: here's a draft timeline template (to copy into postmortems):
```
- Incident opened: t0
- Incident commander assigned: t0 + 15m
- Postmortem draft: t0 + 48h
- Remediation triage into queue: t0 + 72h
- Sprintlet assignment window: next monday 09:00 (owner assigned)
- Fix target by severity: P1 7d, P2 21d, P3 backlog
- Review & close: once fix validated & doc updated
```

mike: +1. also add 'regression signal' tag for recurring items so they get priority.

aya: operational detail — the queue could live in the incident tracker (label=remediation-queue) and we add a 'sprintlet' field. can we automate owner rotation assignment? maybe a small lambda.

sam: yes, automation plan: on monday 09:00 run job, pick N owners from oncall pool, assign up to M tasks each, post a summary to #eng-oncall.

lisa: one more ask: include a lightweight retro 2 weeks post-fix to check for recurrence. keep it 20 minutes.

mike: I'll prototype the automation script. sam, can you add the template to the runbook? i'll wire the labels.

sam: will do. filing a follow-up ticket to the ops repo now. thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: follow-up ticket created: OPS-4821
